# Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI

**Company:** Quillstone Payments (fictional name; card-payment and business-tools provider)
**Location:** Hamburg, Germany (office-first)
**Team:** AI team within Customer Operations

## About the team

The Customer Operations organisation wants merchants to get help quickly and without friction. The AI team builds models and assistants that answer merchant questions, route tickets and help support agents. You will work with backend engineers, data scientists and product managers to take ideas from prototype to production.

## What you will do

- Build, deploy and operate AI and machine learning systems used by the support organisation
- Maintain pipelines for data processing, training and serving
- Fine-tune and evaluate models, including language models, for accuracy and cost
- Prepare and clean large text datasets
- Apply normal engineering discipline: version control, CI/CD and automated tests
- Integrate ML components into the wider product with other engineering teams

## Requirements

- Degree in machine learning, computer science or a related engineering field
- At least four years of experience as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production
- Experience with AI products such as chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
- Software engineering skills for production systems: model serving, monitoring, data versioning
- Experience with a major cloud provider (AWS, GCP or Azure)
- Strong Python; familiarity with MLOps and orchestration tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or an LLM-observability tool
- Experience with feature engineering and data ingestion pipelines

## Benefits

- Annual learning budget, employee share programme and company pension contribution
- Relocation support and subsidised meals
- Sabbatical after several years of service

Dear Thistlebox Data Team,

I am applying for the Data Scientist role.

At Firth Energy Retail I work as a junior data analyst, where I segment customers and analyse tariffs in R and SQL. I automated our monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, which saved the team about two days each month.

My MSc in Statistics, with a dissertation on Bayesian hierarchical models, gave me a strong foundation in experimental design and modelling uncertainty. I would love to apply this to a fast-moving consumer business where experiments drive decisions every week.

I have been learning Python to complement R, and I am comfortable with pandas and scikit-learn.

Thank you for considering my application.

Kind regards,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

company_info.company_description:
Quillstone Payments is a privately held financial-services company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Hamburg. It builds payment and money-management tools for small merchants, including card terminals, a point-of-sale app and a business account; it has also added a personal account for merchants’ customers. The company serves millions of merchants across Europe and the Americas, with around 2,500 employees across roughly 20 offices.

Quillstone’s culture combines team autonomy with shared principles rather than heavy process. Teams own their services and work across product, engineering and operations to solve merchants’ problems. Its stated values are taking ownership, putting the team first, and learning from mistakes. The company also emphasizes pragmatism, humility, candid feedback and openly sharing context. It is office-first, with some flexibility agreed by teams, and supports professional growth through development plans, training budgets, peer feedback and internal tech talks. Quillstone also supports local business education projects and publishes an annual inclusion report.

My weekly recipe-demand forecast uses LightGBM and engineered calendar, price and menu-position features; scheduling it through Vertex AI Workbench to write results to BigQuery helped improve WAPE from 23% to 14%, with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste.

I have also developed a weekly XGBoost churn-scoring workflow in BigQuery using dbt, and built a Streamlit calculator for planning and analysing sequential A/B tests, now used by around 25 colleagues in product and growth. I wrote the calculator’s Dockerfile, and I began adding pytest unit tests to forecasting feature code in 2025, reaching approximately 60% coverage. My experience so far has focused on scheduled and batch workflows rather than serving models through an API; I am now looking to grow toward machine-learning engineering and deepen my experience building production systems.

Quillstone’s focus on helping merchants and its close collaboration across AI, engineering, product and operations make this role particularly appealing. I would bring a strong foundation in Python, feature engineering, statistics and applied machine learning, along with experience translating analytical work into tools and workflows that colleagues can use. I hold an MSc in Statistics, with a dissertation on Bayesian hierarchical models, and have also completed a personal image-classification course project using PyTorch.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to Quillstone’s Customer Operations AI team.

Kind regards,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, well structured and supported by specific evidence. The quantified forecasting result, food-waste estimate, user adoption, test coverage and MSc are effective. It is also unusually transparent about the limits of the candidate's production engineering experience, which protects credibility. However, the paragraph beginning “My experience so far...” gives substantial emphasis to missing experience and weakens the persuasive flow. The closing is also somewhat generic and could connect the candidate's proven experience in operational ML workflows more specifically to Quillstone's Customer Operations AI work without claiming unsupported chatbot, RAG or model-serving experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The plain-text structure is ATS-friendly: standard paragraphs, no tables, graphics or unusual formatting, and clear role/company references. Relevant terms such as Python, feature engineering, LightGBM, XGBoost, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt, Docker, pytest, batch workflows and experimentation are present. AI screening probability is moderate rather than high because several core terms from the advertisement are absent or only indirectly represented, including Google Cloud Platform (GCP), model serving, monitoring, data versioning, MLOps, orchestration, chat assistants and RAG. The missing terms relating to chat/RAG, serving, monitoring and data versioning reflect genuine experience gaps and should not be added. The document could, however, use the supported exact term “GCP” alongside Vertex AI Workbench and BigQuery.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role's Python, applied machine learning, feature engineering, cloud and scheduled/batch workflow aspects. The forecasting and churn examples demonstrate measurable operational impact, and the testing and Docker details provide some evidence of software-engineering discipline. The candidate's experience also supports the company's emphasis on practical, cross-functional work through tools used by product and growth colleagues. Major requirement gaps remain: the candidate has an MSc in Statistics rather than a clearly specified machine learning, computer science or engineering degree; has worked as a Data Scientist rather than as a Machine Learning Engineer for four years; has no stated chat-assistant or RAG experience; and has not independently delivered API model serving, monitoring or data versioning. The candidate also does not have the named MLOps tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow or Airflow. These are genuine fit gaps, not defects that can be solved by rewriting. The material does support GCP exposure through BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench, strong Python, feature engineering and scheduled/batch workflows.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None. The cover letter contains no unsupported skills, tools or experience requiring correction.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the first paragraph, change “scheduling it through Vertex AI Workbench to write results to BigQuery” to “using Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including Vertex AI Workbench and BigQuery, to schedule the workflow and make its results available for operational use.” This adds the supported ATS term “GCP” while accurately describing the candidate's experience without implying broad GCP infrastructure expertise.

2. In the second paragraph, replace the two sentences beginning “My experience so far has focused on scheduled and batch workflows...” with: “My current work has centred on scheduled and batch machine-learning workflows, and I am now seeking to extend that foundation into production machine-learning engineering and reliable operational systems.” This preserves the truthful distinction between existing experience and the intended transition while avoiding a paragraph that reads primarily as a list of deficiencies.

3. In the final paragraph, replace “I would bring a strong foundation in Python, feature engineering, statistics and applied machine learning, along with experience translating analytical work into tools and workflows that colleagues can use” with “I would bring strong Python, feature engineering, statistics and applied machine-learning experience, including translating models and analysis into operational workflows and tools used by colleagues.” This uses the advertisement's terminology more directly and ties the claim to the forecasting, churn and Streamlit examples already described.

4. In the final paragraph, replace the generic sentence “Quillstone’s focus on helping merchants and its close collaboration across AI, engineering, product and operations make this role particularly appealing” with “Quillstone’s focus on helping merchants, and the opportunity to apply practical machine-learning workflows within Customer Operations, make this role particularly appealing.” This creates a more specific connection to the advertised team without claiming experience with support assistants or RAG.
